messages.subject: Re: shinyapps.io- Failed to load resource: the server responded with a status of 500 (Internal Server Error)
messages.subject_clean: shinyapps.io- Failed to load resource: the server responded with a status of 500 (Internal Server Error)
messages.body_plain:
The problem in my case ended up being that I had run out of system memory, which can be solved by upping the allowed memory: shinyapps::configureApp("APPNAME", size="xlarge")

where "APPNAME" is the name of the app. More info about memory is here:http://shiny.rstudio.com/articles/shinyapps.html

Thanks to the folks at RStudio for helping diagnose.

messages.body_plain:
Hi everyone,

I have a problem with one of the tabs in my app that uses googleVis motionchart:
https://hstojic.shinyapps.io/popularity/
Step by step tab

It seems to be really slow to load and almost always the screen gets greyish color, as what happens when you start the application locally and then shut down the process in R console. When the inputs change a different portion of the data set is loaded in and motionchart is made. After experimenting with loading time, I divided the big data set in many smaller ones that are then loaded depending on the inputs. It was taking less time than loading the big data set (55 milions of rows) and then subsetting it. I ended up with each data set being 100000 rows, which is somewhat big, but I would not say really huge, certainly comparable with other shiny+motioncharts examples I have seen out there. I tried increasing the size of the instance and that does not help. I tried rearranging the code so that motionchart is saved as an R object instead of the data set and then it is loaded when inputs change, and it did not help (you can see it on https://hstojic.shinyapps.io/popularitySearch).

Anybody had similar issues?

Best,
Hrvoje

messages.subject: Re: [shinyapps-users] Why does my shiny app status is sleeping in the dashboard?
messages.subject_clean: [shinyapps-users] Why does my shiny app status is sleeping in the dashboard?
messages.body_plain:
Livan,

You will find that the application with continually move from sleeping into running. This is because the application is put to sleep automatically when no users are using it. Conversely, it is automatically woken up when someone visits it (you can observe this when you see the "please wait" page). This has been the behavior of ShinyApps for some time, the only change is we now correctly display the status of the application.

-Andy

Hello,
The shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io/> service suffered an outage last night. The issue has since been resolved as of this morning at noon (EST).  The problem was caused by an automatic update of a package on our load balancers which caused our load balancers to intermittently fail. We have eliminated the automatic updates and added additional monitoring to alert us of these conditions in the future.   If you are still seeing any issues with the service, please don't hesitate to reach out.
Apologies for the disruption and thank you for your patience with us.

--Chad Barraford
Software Engineer @ RStudio

My app displays an interactive plot via renderUI. The code that creates the interactive plot generates and prints a ggplot object to a temporary pdf file as a byproduct. This seems to fail on shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io> but I cannot reproduce the error locally.

Is there something I am missing about how graphics devices work on shinyapps? I assumed that the pdf() function with dev.off() would work on any R installation. The error I am getting is

error in evaluating the argument 'group' in selecting a method for function 'devStartGroup': Error in if (isUTF8) { : missing value where TRUE/FALSE needed Calls: devGrob ... devGrob.viewport -> getID -> prefixName -> paste0 -> escapeSelector

The app is hosted here: https://sachsmc.shinyapps.io/plotROC/
And the code can be seen here: https://github.com/sachsmc/plotROC/tree/master/inst/shinyApp

Any insight would be greatly appreciated.

  library(shiny)
  library(ggplot2)
  library(grid)
  library(gridSVG)

  output$test <- renderUI({

      p <- ggplot(mtcars, aes(x = mpg, y = hp)) + geom_point(size = 5) +
        scale_y_continuous(limits = c(-50, 500)) + scale_x_continuous(limits = c(0, 50))

      pdf(file = tempfile(fileext = ".pdf"), width = 7, height = 5)
      print(p)

      grid.force()

      tmpFile <- tempfile()
      svgString <- gridSVG::grid.export(name = tmpFile, prefix = "cars")$svg
      svgString <- paste(readLines(tmpFile, warn = FALSE), collapse = "\n")
      dev.off()

      HTML(svgString)

  })

}))

Perhaps this a workaround:

localeToCharset <- function() { "UTF-8" }

messages.body_plain:
Hi

I've been running a shiny server for a couple of months and I'm having the same problem with an app since last week. it starts ok and does its things pretty well for a while, but suddenly when asked to update it just stops with no warning or error. is it possible there is something wrong with the last update of the shiny package? I also found a few posts about data.table that can't handle too many data in a join when using it in a shiny app. Actually, I have three data.tables in my app, ~300th, ~160th and ~90th rows, and one reactive fun contains a join on two of them.

Thanks,
Luca

messages.subject: How to prevent "error: cannot open the connection" when users try to upload data?
messages.subject_clean: How to prevent "error: cannot open the connection" when users try to upload data?
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

I have created a shiny app where users can upload .csv files and then apply some network analysis methods to the data.

The problem I am having is that when the user tries to upload a file, the error "Error: cannot open the connection" appears. This does not happen when I run the app locally, and it does not happen when the user selects one of the demo files that I have included in the app.

The way I have allowed users to upload data is with the line:

> read.csv(file.choose(),header=TRUE,check.names=FALSE)

or in another case:

> read.csv(file.choose(),header=TRUE,row.names=1,check.names=FALSE)

I am not sure how to get around this issue, and would appreciate any help at all!

Best regards,
Julia

messages.subject: Re: [shinyapps-users] How to prevent "error: cannot open the connection" when users try to upload data?
messages.subject_clean: [shinyapps-users] How to prevent "error: cannot open the connection" when users try to upload data?
messages.body_plain:
Hi Julia,
The file.choose() functionality assumes that the file is already on disk.  In your local environment, you have the file there, in the cloud version, you need to handle the upload.  You will want to use something like FileInput <http://shiny.rstudio.com/reference/shiny/latest/fileInput.html> and then write your code to take the file that was uploaded and use that instead.

Hope this helps.
-Tareef

messages.body_plain:
Ken,

Thanks for sending the files.

I did a quick check, but didn't have time to go through it thoroughly.

When I run your application locally, after changing the absolute paths to relative paths, I see the error on changing directory. So this is not a problem only on shinyapps. Do you not see any errors running locally?
This points to the fact that your current directory changes during the application run. I added a little output of getwd() to the first page, and verified that your current directory in fact changes.
So it seems that the function(s) that set the directory to a directory within your application gets called again. The first time the call is successful, but any subsequent time, this will cause error as your current directory has already changed. So setwd with absolute path will always work, but with relative path will only work once, unless you set it back to the top level. I didn't get deep into your code, and can't tell where/how to set it back. You would know better. Or alternatively, do not use setwd(), but access the data and function files using a relative path.

Hope this helps!

Best,
Fereshteh

On Thursday, October 23, 2014 1:45:33 PM UTC-4, Fereshteh Karimeddini wrote:
> Ken,
>
> Thanks for sending the files.
>
> I did a quick check, but didn't have time to go through it thoroughly.
>
> When I run your application locally, after changing the absolute paths to relative paths, I see the error on changing directory. So this is not a problem only on shinyapps. Do you not see any errors running locally?
> This points to the fact that your current directory changes during the application run. I added a little output of getwd() to the first page, and verified that your current directory in fact changes.
> So it seems that the function(s) that set the directory to a directory within your application gets called again. The first time the call is successful, but any subsequent time, this will cause error as your current directory has already changed. So setwd with absolute path will always work, but with relative path will only work once, unless you set it back to the top level. I didn't get deep into your code, and can't tell where/how to set it back. You would know better. Or alternatively, do not use setwd(), but access the data and function files using a relative path.
>
> Hope this helps!
>
> Best,
> Fereshteh
>
> On Thursday, October 23, 2014 12:50:41 PM UTC-4, Ken Takagi wrote:
> > Sorry, there was a slight error in the filepaths for setwd() and source().  I've corrected it and re-attached the zip.  This shouldn't change the behavior I was experiencing though.

> > > I've attached a .zip that has the ui.R, server.R, a directory with functions ("functions"), and the directory with the data ("IsoData"), which actually contains a subfolder with the actual data file.  I've only included 4 data files, but typically I have 100s.  Hopefully my scripts aren't too confusing.   Let me know if you need more explanation.  I was able to get this to run locally, so it should work.
> > >
> > > I've commented the lines where I use setwd() or sources() (for calling the functions).  Right now they are set to the absolute filepaths I mentioned in my earlier post (ie. /srv/...).

> > > >
> > > > setwd() should work, depending on how you use it.
> > > > Do you mind sharing your code with us?

> > > > Thanks,
> > > > Fereshteh
> > > >
> > > > On Wednesday, October 22, 2014 7:52:07 PM UTC-4, Ken Takagi wrote:
> > > > > After searching the showLogs() for my app, I was able to figure out what was going on.  My data directory was in the right location, and it was being uploaded to the server, but for some reason using relative file paths to change the working directory was not work for me.
> > > > >
> > > > > Using the absolute file path setwd("/srv/shiny-server/MyApp/MyData") worked, but relative filepaths setwd("./MyData") did not work.  Its a little strange because when I run deployApp(), the function warnings me that I'm using absolute paths, and I should use relative file paths instead.  Not sure if this is a bug or not.
> > > > >
> > > > > On Wednesday, October 22, 2014 3:41:25 PM UTC-4, Ken Takagi wrote:
> > > > > > I'm attempted to deploy my first app on shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io>.  In the app, the user selects a file from a drop down menu, and the data file is plotted.   I am confused where to put the directory with the data so that the app can access it; I keep getting the "ERROR: Cannot change working directory" message.
> > > > > >
> > > > > > My directory is like so:  server.R, ui.R and data directory (called MyData) are located in /MyShinyApp.  When I deploy the app using deployApp() (which works fine), a directory called shinyapps is created in /MyShinyApp, with a subdirectory /MyUsername which contains a MyShinyApp.dcf file.  I am using the follow relative path to tell the app where my data is: setwd("./MyData").  Any suggestions on where to move the MyData directory so that my app can access it?

> > > > > > Thanks in advance.

Hi Tareef,
thanks for the link btw my point was that there could be a much simpler way to allow users to share data across sessions with ShinyApps.io other than the 3 mentioned in the article since some users may find them cumbersome as per the article's comments.

An easier way would require an enhancement to the deployApp() function simply allowing to download all data files from the server first and reuploading soon after (download data - deploy - reupload data).

Hopefully people at RStudio can think about it

messages.subject: Re: [shinyapps-users] Share data across sessions with ShinyApps.io
messages.subject_clean: [shinyapps-users] Share data across sessions with ShinyApps.io
messages.body_plain:
This approach won't work; log.txt will not be preserved even between redeploys. Once your app goes idle (i.e. no users are connected) ShinyApps may decide at any time to shut it down until the next user shows up, and when that happens any changes you made on disk will be lost. Even if we didn't do that, your app may be deployed on multiple different servers, the copy of log.txt you download would depend on which server you happened to hit at that exact moment.

I do think we need to offer a solution to this problem that's easier than the ones we have today, but at the moment the ones in the article you linked to are what you need to do.

messages.subject_clean: [shinyapps-users] showcase mode - any way to interactively turn on/off?
messages.body_plain:
Hi Cliff -

I don't think there's a way to toggle showcase mode for a given application session (that is, without reloading the page), but you could display the page with "?showcase=0" at the end of the URL to disable the showcase display.

For example, here's one from the gallery with and without showcase:
https://gallery.shinyapps.io/006-tabsets/
https://gallery.shinyapps.io/006-tabsets/?showcase=0

Note that you can only disable the showcase this way for an app that has it enabled in the DESCRIPTION with "DisplayMode: Showcase" -- you can't enable showcase with this for an app that doesn't have it enabled in the DESCRIPTION.

-Winston

Your memories are partially correct.  Once the service moves out of Beta, the free tier will not support authenticated applications.  That would be a paid tier that you could consider if you were interested in hosting your application on shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io>. -Tareef

messages.subject: Re: [shinyapps-users] shinyapps.io session
messages.subject_clean: [shinyapps-users] shinyapps.io session
messages.body_plain:
Hi David,
The model for running on shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io> is different than Spark. Whereas Spark configured an RStudio server to allow you to do the work right on the server, shinyapps presumes that you will get the work done anywhere, and you will deploy your application to production.

I would recommend starting up your R process (base R or through the IDE), install the packages that are recommended, and when you have your app ready for deployment, you can deploy it directly from the console.

Hope this helps
Tareef
